newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chips fall as investors take profits.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips fall as investors take profits.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell Wednesday as investors took profits and paused to assess the market's next move after its recent dizzying rise into the record books.
The Dow Jones industrial average lost 26.18 points to close at 7,357.23, a day after jumping 38 points to a record 7,383.41, its sixth milestone this month and the 21st of the year.
But the Nasdaq composite index eked out a gain of 0.97 of a point to 1,410.18, topping Tuesday's record as investors were again drawn to high-technology and some smaller stocks.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,310 to 1,150 on active volume of 487 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts said investors who have been buying blue-chips turned cautious as interest rates kept rising in the bond market.

"For the last few days, people thought short-term rates were not going to rise, but they edged up. That can hurt equities performance," said Michael Metz, chief investment officer at Oppenheimer & Co.
"A lot of portfolio managers are peeling back their blue chip holdings a little, because they have run very far, very fast," said Metz.
The yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury stayed above 7 percent, a level that tends to draw funds away from stocks.

Investors were also trying to make sense of the latest economic data. The government said orders for costly manufactured goods rose in April after falling in March but lower order backlogs pointed to slower growth ahead.
The Commerce Department said durable goods orders rose 1.4 percent, the third increase in the past four months, following a revised 2.2 percent drop in March.
The report fit with other signs that the economy was losing some momentum in the second-quarter after a sizzling 5.6 percent rate of expansion in the first quarter.

Analysts detected an improved outlook for the networking stocks. Among the group, 3Com Corp. jumped 4-3/8 to 51-1/8 and U.S. Robotics Corp. rose 7-3/4 to 88-1/2. FORE Systems Inc. was up 1-7/8 to 16-5/8.
International Business Machines Corp. was up 1/2 at 89-7/8 after its 2-for-1 stock split.
Nike Inc. B shares rose 3-5/8 to 63-5/8 on lingering speculation that billionaire investor Warren Buffett favours the sports marketing giant as an investment.

Charles Schwab Corp. gained 2-7/8 to 38-3/4. The discount brokerage firm's stock was added to the Standard & Poor's 500 Index so all mutual funds that track that index quickly poured money to shift their investments into Schwab.
HFS Inc. tumbled 4 to 54-1/2 and CUC International Inc. lost 2-3/4 at 23-1/4 a day after the companies announced an $11 billion stock-swap merger.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks slipped 2.50 points to 847.21. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.35 to 600.79.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 1.01 to 439.66. The average share was down 10 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,013.048 down 13.549 or 0.17 percent.
